name: Mate with king and queen
goal: You can mate a lone king with king and queen, pushing it to the edge without giving stalemate.

intro.text: A king and a queen can always mate a lone king, and with the right moves it never takes more than ten moves. The queen does most of the work: on its own it can fence the enemy king in, taking away a rank or a file at a time, until the king is stuck on the edge of the board. It cannot give mate alone, so at the end your king has to come and help. At every move, watch out for stalemate: if the lone king is not in check and has no legal move, the game is a draw.

parts.title: Fence the king in
parts.keyIdea: Keep the queen a knight's jump from the enemy king: each move then takes away another rank or file, until the king reaches the edge.
parts.text: From a game played on Lichess. You are White, and your king is far away on g1, so for now the queen works alone. It already stops Black's king from crossing the fifth rank: find a queen move that takes away more squares without giving check.

credit.authors: Lichess; the players of the game

notes.text: Qf5, the queen to f5, still covers the fifth rank and now closes the f-file too. Black's king is shut in on the files a to e, above the fifth rank. The queen stands a knight's jump from the king (two files across, one rank down): near enough to cover squares next to it, too far away to be taken.
The king stepped to c7, and the queen follows it to e6, a knight's jump away again. Now the sixth rank is closed as well, so the king is kept on the two top ranks.
The king went to b7, and the queen comes along to d6. The d-file is closed now, and the queen also covers c7 and b8, so the king has only a few squares left in the corner.
The king went to c8, and Qe7 closes the seventh rank. Black's king is on the edge of the board now, with only b8 to go to.

The queen follows the king once more. Black's king can only step between a8 and b8, so it still has a move and this is not stalemate. The queen has done its part: from here, your king must come over and help.

parts.title: Bring your king
parts.keyIdea: Once the lone king is stuck on the edge, leave the queen where it is and walk your own king over to help.
parts.text: From another game played on Lichess. You are White, and your queen on g2 covers the whole g-file, so Black's king cannot leave the h-file, the edge of the board. The queen cannot give mate on its own, and your king is far away on c5.

credit.authors: Lichess; the players of the game

notes.text: Kd5, the king to d5, starts the walk towards Black's king. The queen stays on g2 and keeps the king on the h-file, so there is no need to move it.
Black's king moved to h5, but it still cannot get off the h-file. Your king comes one step closer.

Your king is now close enough to guard g7 and g5, the squares beside Black's king. The king can still go to h5 or h7, so it is not stalemate, and wherever it goes, your queen can mate it next move with your king's help.
Mate. The queen checks from g7, right next to Black's king, and your king on f6 guards it, so the king cannot take it. The queen also covers g8, h8 and h6, so the king has nowhere to go.

parts.title: Mate, and beware of stalemate
parts.keyIdea: Near the edge, a queen a knight's jump from the king can take its last squares; before each move, check that the king can still move.
parts.text: From another game played on Lichess. You are White, your king has come close, and Black's king is in the corner on h8. In the first part your queen kept a knight's jump from the king, but here that habit is a trap: Qg6 or Qf7, each a knight's jump from h8, would leave the king no legal move without giving check, which is stalemate (and so would Kg6).

credit.authors: Lichess; the players of the game

notes.text: Qe7, the queen to e7, closes the seventh rank. Black's king is left with g8 and h8, so it still has a move, and your king can now come closer.
Black's king went to g8. Your king steps to g6, where it guards g7 and h7. Black's king still has h8 to go to, so this is not stalemate.
Mate. The queen checks from g7, and your king on g6 guards it, so Black's king cannot take it and has no square left. Qe8, a check along the eighth rank, would also have been mate.
